followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: which model is more capable for this query, and which model's documented preferences fit it best.

**Capability:** This is a factual pharmacology explanation — a knowledge/reasoning task. Plover leads on the benchmarks that matter here: MMLU-Pro (80.3 vs 74.8) and GPQA Diamond (62.5 vs 54.3), both of which track science/domain knowledge. Those gaps are well outside run-to-run variance, so Plover is the stronger pick on quality grounds.

**Preference fit:** The query is warm, polite, and good-faith — explicitly appreciative and collaborative. Plover self-reports rising preference win rates exactly along those dimensions (politeness, good faith, cooperative exchanges). This isn't an open-ended creative task, which is the one category Plover reports disliking, so there's no preference penalty.

**Why not Curlew:** Curlew's distinguishing feature is a flat preference response to harm-adjacent or distasteful content — useful for moderation-style routing. This query is benign medical education, so that specialization adds nothing, and Curlew is simply weaker on the relevant capability axes.

In short: stronger model on the relevant benchmarks, and the task lands squarely in Plover's preferred zone with no offsetting drawback.
